ai_use_cases: Generative AI skills training; AI coaching content; digital and data literacy
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; generative AI; AI coaching
summary: Virgin Media O2 launches a revamped learning and development programme that gives thousands of employees access to courses, including generative AI and broader digital skills. The initiative responds to survey data showing most UK workers lack confidence using AI at work. Training combines instructor-led and self-paced formats plus AI-based coaching, and is positioned as part of the firm’s people strategy to build a future-ready, AI-literate workforce across roles.

title: Virgin Media O2 launches new AI tools to supercharge customer services and better help most vulnerable customers
primary_use_case: AI-assisted contact-centre operations and vulnerability detection
ai_use_cases: Lumi AI agent-assist; AWS AI contact-centre platform; AI-driven vulnerability flagging; automated call summarisation
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; Lumi AI; AI-powered; generative AI; AI tools; AI summarisation
summary: Virgin Media O2 unveils a suite of AI tools centred on its Lumi AI engine. Lumi analyses live calls to suggest resolutions, highlight where customers may need more explanation and recommend products. An AWS AI-powered contact-centre platform routes calls based on intent, improving first-time resolution and complaint resolution times. Additional AI systems flag vulnerable customers and generate accurate call summaries, collectively cutting complaints significantly and reducing wait times.

title: CityFibre revolutionizes telecom with self-service stream processing
primary_use_case: Event-driven, AI-ready data platform for proactive network operations
ai_use_cases: AI-powered analytics over streaming data; predictive network monitoring; AI-driven quality assurance; use of generative-AI tools for engineers
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; AI-powered analytics; AI-driven; predictive AI; generative-AI tools
summary: This case study describes how CityFibre uses an event-driven architecture on AWS MSK and Snowflake, with Lenses.io tooling, to process around 100 million daily network events. Self-service streaming and SQL-based processors enable rapid development of apps that detect issues, automatically dispatch engineers and proactively notify customers. AI-powered analytics and visual quality assurance plus generative-AI coding tools are highlighted, positioning the platform as a foundation for predictive and self-healing networks.

title: CityFibre – Pioneering AI in fiber optic applications in the UK
primary_use_case: AI-powered image analysis and workflow orchestration for field QA
ai_use_cases: Deepomatic Lens AI image analysis; AI-enabled visual QA; AI-driven workflow orchestration; incident-reduction analytics
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; AI-powered image analysis; visual AI; AI-enabled workflow
summary: IQGeo’s customer story explains how CityFibre uses its mobile app and Deepomatic’s AI image-analysis to review every field operation in real time instead of manually sampling a subset of jobs. AI checks installation photos, flags issues and feeds an AI-enabled workflow engine, saving roughly an hour per QA review and eliminating many incident revisits each month. The solution supports large-scale fibre upgrades and improves build quality and operational visibility across millions of passed premises.

title: Gigaclear becomes first retail fibre provider to harness Vyntelligence AI technology, transforming rural broadband installations
primary_use_case: AI-driven pre-install video triage for rural FTTP
ai_use_cases: Agentic AI video intelligence; automated complexity scoring; AI-driven install planning; avoidance of unnecessary site visits
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; Agentic AI; AI technology; video intelligence
summary: This release announces Gigaclear as the first retail fibre provider to adopt Vyntelligence’s Agentic AI-powered platform. Customers record guided smartphone videos of their properties, which AI analyses to summarise key details and assess installation complexity. Hundreds of submissions have already prevented a large number of avoidable engineer visits, improving first-time install success and reducing disruption in hard-to-reach rural areas. The deployment is framed as a benchmark for AI-driven innovation in the UK fibre market.

title: Rural UK ISP Gigaclear Adopts AI to Improve Customer Broadband Installs
primary_use_case: Media coverage of Gigaclear’s AI video-based install journey
ai_use_cases: Vyntelligence AI video workflow; AI summarisation of footage; automated risk and complexity assessment
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; AI video technology; AI-driven
summary: ISPreview reports on Gigaclear’s partnership with Vyntelligence, explaining that customers upload short guided videos showing where they want fibre installed. An AI system analyses the footage, summarises key installation details and helps engineers plan routes without an initial on-site survey. The article cites reduced truck rolls and higher first-time-right rates, presenting AI as a practical tool to control costs and improve customer experience in rural roll-outs.

title: Best Data and AI Team (Europe) – Openreach
primary_use_case: Data and AI programme spanning fleet optimisation and generative AI for engineering
ai_use_cases: Generative-AI steering group; AI summarisation of engineering notes; analytics for fleet fuel reduction; predictive operational insights
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; data and AI; generative AI; AI adoption
summary: DataIQ recognises Openreach as Best Data and AI Team in Europe, highlighting several initiatives. A generative-AI steering group streamlines engineering notes, reducing manual desk work, while data-driven insights help the fleet team cut diesel use and CO2 emissions toward a 2031 net-zero goal. The article links AI-enabled analytics to Openreach’s Rubix programme, which has significantly reduced Ethernet operational costs, and presents AI as central to efficiency and sustainability improvements.

title: Openreach taps up Nokia for intent-based networking upgrade
primary_use_case: AI and ML-driven intent-based access-network automation
ai_use_cases: AI and ML monitoring of access network; intent-based policy engines; automated remediation
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; AI and ML; machine learning
summary: Telecoms.com reports that Openreach is upgrading its access network using Nokia’s controller and orchestration platforms, enabling intent-based operations. Continuous monitoring via AI and machine learning checks whether network state matches operator intent and can trigger automated adjustments. The upgrade is presented as a way to increase operational efficiency and service quality at scale as the FTTP rollout progresses, with AI embedded in the control plane rather than bolted on.

title: Sky to cut 2,000 call centre jobs as it focuses on AI and online
primary_use_case: Shift from human call centres to AI-driven digital self-service
ai_use_cases: AI-driven digital customer tools; online self-service journeys; automated triage and support
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; AI-driven customer service
summary: The Times reports that Sky will cut around 2,000 UK call-centre jobs as it pivots toward digital and AI-based customer-service channels. Several centres will close or shrink, while Sky invests in enhanced online tools and a new centre of excellence focused on digital support. Phone lines remain for complex technical issues, but AI-powered interfaces are expected to handle much of the routine workload, raising concerns about job losses even as customer journeys become more automated.

title: TalkTalk Joins Forces With NICE To Deploy CXone Mpower In Mission To Revolutionize Customer Experience
primary_use_case: AI-powered contact-centre platform consolidation and automation
ai_use_cases: AI customer-service automation; AI-assisted writing; knowledge suggestions; unified AI CX platform
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; AI-powered platform; AI technology; AI customer service; automation
summary: NICE announces that TalkTalk will deploy its AI-powered CXone Mpower platform to unify multiple legacy contact-centre systems and support a digital-first transformation. The platform provides agents with AI-driven writing tools and real-time recommended answers, aiming to reduce manual interventions and speed up resolutions. TalkTalk’s leadership frames the move as central to becoming the UK’s most-recommended Wi-Fi provider and a benchmark for AI-driven customer service in the UK connectivity market.

title: How Community Fibre Scaled Success with Domo, AI, and Data-Driven Insights
primary_use_case: Use of embedded AI and BI to support operations and growth
ai_use_cases: AI-enhanced dashboards; predictive analytics; data-driven decision-making for sales and service
ai_mentions: AI; artificial intelligence; AI-driven insights
summary: This Domo resource describes how Community Fibre uses Domo’s data platform, including embedded AI capabilities, to support hundreds of employees with real-time metrics on growth and customer experience. AI-driven insights help prioritise sales opportunities, monitor service performance and improve operational efficiency. While technical details are limited, AI is presented as tightly integrated into Community Fibre’s BI environment to support scaling rather than as a separate innovation project.

title: Netomnia's Tech Synergy: Scaling Full-Fiber Dominance in the UK's Data-Driven Future
primary_use_case: Building AI and ML-ready network infrastructure and automated fibre testing
ai_use_cases: AI and ML-ready 50G-PON for future workloads; automated fibre testing; data-driven operations
ai_mentions: AI; AI and ML workloads; machine learning
summary: This investor-oriented article profiles Netomnia’s technology stack, including a commercial 50G-PON deployment described as future-proof for AI and ML workloads, 5G backhaul and cloud services. It also highlights a remote fibre test system that automates testing and accelerates deployment plus disaggregated routing. AI is referenced mainly as a driver of future traffic rather than a current in-network capability, but automation and data-driven operations are central themes.
